objective.statement: Add request logging to every endpoint in src/api/ for audit purposes, such that the logging adds zero measurable latency and never logs request bodies, which contain PII.
objective.success_definition: Every endpoint in src/api/ produces audit request logs; the logging adds zero measurable latency to request handling; and no request body content ever appears in the logs.

goals.statement: Add request logging to every endpoint in src/api/ for audit purposes.
acceptance: A request log entry is produced for every request handled by every endpoint under src/api/.
The log entries serve the stated audit purpose.

goals.statement: Ensure the request logging adds zero measurable latency.
acceptance: No measurable latency difference in endpoint request handling is attributable to the logging.

goals.statement: Ensure request bodies are never logged, because they contain PII.
acceptance: No request body content appears in any log output, for any endpoint or request type.

constraints.statement: The logging must add zero measurable latency to request handling.
Request bodies must never be logged, because they contain PII.
Logging must cover every endpoint in src/api/.

assumptions.statement: "Every endpoint in src/api/" means all request handlers defined under the src/api/ directory tree.
"Zero measurable latency" will be validated by comparing endpoint latency with and without the logging enabled.
Audit log entries will contain non-body request metadata (e.g., method, path, status code, timestamp), since the task does not specify log content beyond excluding bodies.

open_questions.question: What fields should each audit log entry contain, given that request bodies are excluded?
options: Non-body metadata only: method, path, status code, timestamp
A specific audit schema defined elsewhere

open_questions.question: How should "zero measurable latency" be measured and verified?
options: Benchmark endpoints with and without logging and compare
Manual review of the logging implementation for non-blocking behavior

verification.spec: Exercise each endpoint under src/api/ and confirm that a request log entry is produced for every request.
verification.expected: Every endpoint emits an audit request log entry for each request it handles.

verification.spec: Compare endpoint request-handling latency with the logging enabled versus disabled (or absent).
verification.expected: No measurable latency difference is attributable to the logging.

verification.spec: Review the logging implementation and inspect emitted log output to confirm that no request body content is logged for any endpoint or request type.
verification.expected: No request body content appears in any log output.

deliverables.description: Request logging added to every endpoint in src/api/, implemented so that it adds zero measurable latency and never logs request bodies.

factors: The zero-measurable-latency requirement is stringent and constrains how logging can be implemented.
Request bodies contain PII, so any accidental body logging creates a security/compliance incident.
The change touches every endpoint in src/api/, so a defect would have broad impact across the API surface.
